findings.title: Observer prunes other projects' poll and fault state
findings.description: `RunObserver.observe` rebuilds its state from the entries it is given. It filters `_last_poll`, `_overdue` and `_faulted` to `live = {entry.id for entry in entries}`. The observer is one object shared by every project: `RunnerTenant` builds it once (tenant.py:74) and passes it to each `ProjectTick` (tenant.py:133). Each `ProjectTick` passes only its own project's entries (tick.py `_run_entries`). So ticking project A erases project B's last-poll times and standing poll faults, and the reverse. An empty project erases everything. With two or more projects, every in-flight run is polled on every tick. The `ProcessSettings` docstring says `run_poll_interval_seconds` is the least time between polls (settings.py:83). The default idle wait is 1 s (settings.py:87), so the `sq runs wait` spawn rate can rise by up to about 15×. Standing poll faults are also dropped, so their escalations close and reopen. Every observer test uses a single project, so none of this is caught. Fix: prune against the union of all projects' entries, or key the state per project. Add a two-project test that asserts poll counts.

findings.title: A persistent planner error spins the resident loop
findings.description: The broad catch escalates on the project path, where `raise_project_escalation` returns the open row unchanged and writes nothing (project_escalations.py:58-59). It then returns `(TickResult.COMPLETE, True)` unconditionally. `RunnerTenant.tick` returns that `True`, which contradicts its own docstring (tenant.py:96-99). The host runs `worked = tenant.tick(self) or worked` (host.py:275) and skips the idle wait when `worked` is true (host.py:253-254). So a planner that raises every tick causes back-to-back full tracebacks, one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` per pass, and write-lock churn against the other tenants. Production planners are empty today, so this is dormant, but slice 125 adds them. `tests/runner/test_tenant.py#test_an_unexpected_exception_is_logged_and_the_other_project_still_ticks` asserts `wrote` is true and pins the wrong behavior. Fix: return whether the escalation actually wrote, and consider a backoff.

findings.title: An unconfirmed launch does not replay its standing poll fault
findings.description: The comment at observe.py:92-94 says a poll fault is replayed between polls so its escalation does not close. Only `_confirmed` reads `_faulted` (lines 137-145). In `_unconfirmed`, when the child has exited and the poll is not yet due, the code calls `_still_overdue`, which adds nothing unless the launch is overdue, and returns LAUNCHING. The next `_close_recovered` (tick.py) then closes the `run_observation_failed` escalation. The following poll reopens it. So the escalation opens and closes once per poll interval. `test_a_failed_poll_after_an_exit_is_a_fault_and_the_entry_stays` checks only one tick. The replay test uses an entry with no tracked child, so it takes the confirmed path. Fix: consult `_faulted` on the unconfirmed path too, and add a multi-tick test.

findings.title: Same-kind faults collapse into one stale detail
findings.description: `raise_expected_faults` calls `raise_project_escalation` once per fault. The store returns the already-open row unchanged for the same `(project, kind)` (project_escalations.py:58-59). So if two CF links fail in one tick, only the first one's detail is stored. While the kind keeps recurring, the open row keeps naming whichever fault came first, even after that one has recovered. The docstring says only that a repeat writes nothing; it does not mention the loss. `test_a_failed_link_raises_one_escalation...` covers one link only. Fix: either merge the subjects into the payload on recurrence or key the row on the subject, and add a two-subject test.

findings.title: run_id is read and validated four different ways
findings.description: Four sites read the run id from journal parameters. `observe._observe_one` (lines 127-129) checks `isinstance` and non-empty. `finish._run_id` (finish.py, `#_run_id`) checks `isinstance` only. `launch._text_parameter` (launch.py:166-170) checks both. `faults._in_flight_run_ids` does no check: `str(entry.parameters[PARAM_RUN_ID])` turns a `None` into the string `"None"` and writes it into an operator-facing payload. The coercion is latent because `_launch` always writes a string, but it is the silent fallback the project rules forbid. Fix: one helper next to `PARAM_RUN_ID` in the store, used by all four sites. Put it in the store, because `faults.py` cannot import `launch.py` without a cycle.

findings.title: The Runner has no load-tier test
findings.description: The Python rules require at least one `tests/load/` test for code on the concurrency or environment-layer paths, and CI must gate it. The Runner spawns subprocesses, polls, and bounds each tick by `TickBudget`. The budget tests use a fake clock (`tests/runner/test_budget_coverage.py`), which cannot show a tick overrunning in wall time. None of the files under `tests/load/` mention the runner, and the slice documents do not name a load test. Fix: add a load test with realistic project and run counts that asserts tick wall time against the deadline and the poll count against the interval.

findings.title: faults.py docstring contradicts the module
findings.description: The docstring says "Escalation writes join this module in a later task", but `escalate` and `raise_expected_faults` are already in the file and write to the store. Reword the module docstring to match.

findings.title: A finished node is offered to the planners again on the next tick
findings.description: `journal_issue` and `journal_resolve` never touch `NodeStatus` (journal.py has no reference to it). A COMPLETED finish does not block the node either. So the node stays RUNNABLE. `_decide` excludes only nodes with unresolved entries, and it runs after `_record_finished`, so a node whose run just completed is offered again immediately. Nothing is wrong today because production planners are empty, and the test planners guard themselves (`OncePerNode`, the proof planner's markers). Slice 125's dispatch planner would relaunch finished nodes every tick unless 125 changes the node's status. Flag this to 125.

findings.title: observe.py exceeds the file-size guideline
findings.description: The file is 326 lines against the roughly 300-line guideline. The unconfirmed-launch path (lines 171-249) is a separate concern and could move into its own module. That split would also make finding 3 easier to fix.

findings.title: Journal parameter keys and executable names are split across packages
findings.description: `PARAM_RUN_ID` and `PARAM_CHECKOUT` live in the store (journal_models.py:63-68). `PARAM_PIPELINE` and `PARAM_PARAMS` live in the runner. `SQ_EXECUTABLE` lives in `process`, while `CF_EXECUTABLE` lives in `runner/probes.py`. Consolidate the journal keys in the store.

findings.title: Re-raises at the tenant boundary are not logged with a traceback
findings.description: Rule (a) asks for `logger.exception` before a re-raise. The store and shape errors here are re-raised without it. The CLI maps them to exit codes (cli/main.py:295 and 304). I did not verify whether those branches log a traceback. If they do not, add a log at this point.

findings.title: Some Runner tests overstate what they cover
findings.description: The test monkeypatches `_dispatch` and drives the tick loop from the test body. It shows the exit-code mapping, but not that `amoeba start` exits 15 on a usage error. Separately, `tests/runner/test_budget_coverage.py` imports the private helper `_link` from `runner.test_probes`. Move that helper into `tick_support`.

findings.title: Every subprocess start checks the tick budget first
findings.description: I read the probe loop. Each `cf` command is preceded by `budget.allows_call()`. The same check guards the action loop in `tick.py#ProjectTick._act` and both observer calls at observe.py:146 and observe.py:188. The `Popen` call sits behind the `_act` check.

findings.title: Launch uses an argv list, no shell, and never logs the environment
findings.description: I read `launch()`. The argv is a list with no shell. stdin is DEVNULL. The child inherits the environment, and nothing logs it. Both logs are opened in exclusive mode (`"xb"`), so an earlier attempt's evidence is never overwritten. The module has no logger.
